context: The horizontal axis is input size n, marked from 0 to 14. The vertical axis is function value and has no numerical tick labels. The blue curve is the operation count T(n). The orange curve is c·f(n), the candidate function f(n) scaled by a positive constant c. The figure gives no specific formulas for the functions.
description: A dashed green vertical line marks n₀ where the curves meet between 7 and 8. From 1 to 7, the blue curve fluctuates above the orange curve. Beyond n₀, both curves continue upward, with the orange curve always above the blue one.

frames.explanation: The condition at the bottom states that there is a positive constant c and a threshold n₀ such that T(n) ≤ c·f(n) for every n > n₀. We then write T(n) = O(f(n)) and call f(n) an asymptotic upper bound. It does not matter that T(n) exceeded c·f(n) before the threshold. The curves need not be equal everywhere.
frames.title: Asymptotic upper bounds beyond a threshold

summary: Two curves illustrate the relationship that matters for an asymptotic upper bound: which curve stays above the other after a threshold.
title: Asymptotic upper bounds beyond a threshold
